svg.text: PAGE CACHE — read miss → read hit → dirty write → { writeback | crash }
“a region of RAM, organised in 4 KB pages exactly like the rest of memory, in which the kernel keeps copies
of file data it has recently moved between disk and a program” — worked file: report.dat, fd = 3

g.text: cache slot if resident, else disk
dirty = modified in RAM, not yet
free RAM only — reclaimed on demand
no disk I/O this ACT — track dark
after ACT III, page 0 is: cache = v1 DIRTY · disk = v0 stale → two mutually exclusive futures
trade-off: instant, batched writes (ACT III’s gain) are paid for by the crash window (IV-B’s risk)
fsync(fd) = force this flush now (blocks until done)
O_DIRECT would bypass the cache entirely
power fails while p0 is dirty — RAM is volatile
ACT I · read #1 (MISS) — Program calls read(fd = 3, buf, 1 MB); the request travels to the VFS
VFS cache lookup: pages 0–255 all ABSENT (dashed cells) — this read is a MISS
kernel allocates 256 empty 4 KB cache slots — 1,048,576 B ÷ 4,096 B = 256 pages
disk → cache: all 256 pages copied unchanged at ≈5 ms/block — the slow step (longest dwell)
cache → buf: 1 MB copied at RAM speed, ≈5 µs/page — fast
read #1 returns 1 MB; all 256 cache pages STAY resident and clean after the call
ACT II · read #2 (HIT) — read(fd = 3, buf2, 1 MB); buf2 is a NEW buffer reusing this slot — starts empty
VFS lookup: pages 0–255 all PRESENT — kept from ACT I, reused not rebuilt: a HIT
cache → buf2: 1 MB RAM copy only; the disk ↔ cache track stays DARK — zero disk I/O
read #2 returns 1 MB ≈1000× faster (RAM ≈5 µs vs disk ≈5 ms per block)
ACT III · write — write(fd = 3, newbytes, 512 B at offset 0); request travels to the VFS
VFS locates the page: offset 0 ÷ 4,096 = page 0 — already resident from ACT I
512 B of v1 land in cache p0 → flag flips DIRTY; disk b0 still holds stale v0
write returns at once — nothing touched disk; dirty p0 waits → two futures fork below
FUTURE A — writeback thread wakes seconds later, writes v1 to b0 (≈5 ms) → p0 clean again
FUTURE B — power fails first: dirty p0 lived only in volatile RAM → v1 LOST; disk stale forever
